newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end choppy trading mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end choppy trading mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended choppy, sporadic trading mixed, with the yen working upward on the back of widespread talk of central bank intervention.

Turnover in the yen pit proved brisk, with volume estimated on the price boards at some 25,000 contracts, in trade marked by spurts of activity as rumors circulated that the Bank of Japan had entered to defend the yen.

"It was pretty active, with the BoJ reportedly in twice now to buy yen for dollars," said one floor broker late. But none of the brokers who had heard the rumors said they had any hard evidence that the central bank had actually intervened.
"I think what you've got here is people are unwilling to test the central banks' resolve," said the broker.

Traders also mulled unconfirmed talk which surfaced during the morning that a prominent Washington-based consulting firm had written in a newsletter that the United States would be comfortable with a higher dollar.
The broker, who said his brokerage house subscribed to the consulting service, said the firm's most-recent newsletter contained no such commentary.

During the afternoon, March Canadian dollars eroded gains, under pressure from technical selling after the contract tested and stalled at key resistance of $0.7507 and on talk that the Bank of Canada had intervened to brake the Canadian unit's advance, brokers said.
Sterling gyrated broadly, pressured initially by news that the Bank of England had left U.K. rates unchanged after tame U.K. retail-level inflation data.
The pound chopped around after a news report that a Conservative member of British Parliament had died, leaving Prime Minister John Major with a minority.

March Swiss francs lurched lower, touching a new contract low of $0.7290 as locals hunted unsuccessfully for sell stops, and then sliced losses. One bank was seen buying a total of about 1,000 March Swiss francs on the day.
In the yen pit, an investment bank bought about 1,000 March futures when that contract hurdled Wednesday's high of $0.008640, brokers said.

Currency traders saw muted response to comments by Federal Reserve governor Laurence Meyer, who forecast near-trend U.S. economic growth this year but said he had slightly greater concern about rising inflation than slower growth.
The remarks weighed down U.S. Treasury bonds and equities.

The mark eased early when Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said Thursday that "monetary policy cannot be indifferent" to Germany's "dramatic economic position," which last week's record German jobless data highlighted.
Friday's U.S. November international trade gap is expected to widen to $9.8 billion from $7.99 billion in October.

March yen rose $0.000026 at $0.008660, marks lost $0.0027 to $0.6297, Swiss franc fell $0.0026 to $0.7313, pound fell $0.0040 to $1.6768, Can dollar rose $0.0007 to $0.7491, Aus dollar up $0.0035 at $0.7786, Mex peso fell $0.000125 to $0.123825.
